cards.text: Jesus has just told Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, that the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:9-10). The people are still listening, and Jesus is getting close to Jerusalem. So He tells them a parable, and friend, He's telling this one for a reason.

cards.question: The people listening to Jesus think the kingdom of God is still a long way off.

cards.text: So Jesus starts the story: a man of noble birth heads to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return. Before he goes, he hands ten of his servants ten minas, one each.

cards.question: Before he leaves, what does the man tell his servants to do with the money until he returns?

cards.text: But his subjects hated him, and they send a whole delegation after him with a message. Most folks write an angry email, friend, but these folks booked the TRIP.

cards.question: What message does the subjects' delegation carry after the man?

answers.text: They don't want him ruling over them
They want him to hurry back home
They want his servants in charge

cards.text: Then the man comes back, kingship in hand.

cards.question: The man, now king, calls in the servants he gave the money to, so he can find out what each one earned.

cards.text: The first servant steps up, and his one mina has produced TEN more minas. That's one cookie in the oven and a whole BATCH coming out, and friend, my oven has NEVER done that for me.

cards.question: The master tells the first servant, "Well done, good servant!" He says the servant has been faithful in a very ___ matter.
What reward does the master give the first servant?

answers.text: A seat at the king's table

cards.text: Then the second servant comes forward with his report.

cards.question: The second servant reports that his mina has made ten more minas, the same as the first servant's.

cards.text: His mina has made five minas, and the master gives him authority over five cities.

Then another servant comes in: "Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth." That mina spent the whole time wrapped up and put away, and friend, after my years in the back of a junk drawer, I KNOW how that feels.

cards.question: The servant who laid his mina away in a cloth says he did it because he was afraid of the master.

cards.text: The servant tells the master to his FACE that he's a harsh man who withdraws what he did not deposit and reaps what he did not sow. The master answers, "You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words."

cards.question: The master says that if this servant thought he was harsh, there was one simple thing he could have done with the mina. What is it?

answers.text: Put it in the bank to earn interest
Handed it to a neighbor to keep
Traded it for a small piece of land

cards.text: Then the master gives an order to those standing by: take the mina away from him.

cards.question: The master says to give the mina taken from the fearful servant to the servant who has ___ minas.

cards.text: The people standing by speak up: "Master," they said, "he already has ten!" It's like watching the coworker who just got a raise ALSO win the office raffle.

cards.question: The master answers that everyone who has will be given more. What does he say about the one who does not have?

answers.text: Even what he has will be taken away
He will be given a fresh start
He will be left as he is

cards.question: One group from the start of the story still hasn't been dealt with. Who is the master's last order about?

answers.text: The enemies who didn't want him as king
The people of the distant country
The second servant with five minas

cards.text: His order for them is a heavy one: bring those enemies who were unwilling for him to rule over them, and slay them in front of him. And that's where Jesus ends the parable.
